title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
summary: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
summary: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
summary: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
summary: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.
